hints.content: **Reflective (or line) symmetry** means that we can reflect a figure across a line, and the figure will remain unchanged.

##Reflection over $y=x$

This line goes through two of the opposite corner points $(8, 8)$ and $(-6,-6)$.

Under this transformation, each point on the kite maps to another point which is also on the kite. The kite is *symmetric* over this line.


[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A kite mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The kite has a point at negative six, negative six, a point at negative five, zero, a point at zero, negative five, and a point at eight, eight. The equation y equals X is graphed on the coordinate plane. A dotted line shows the reflection of the kite across the line. The image lies on the pre-image.

hints.content:
##Reflection over $y=-x-5$

Under this transformation, some points on the kite map to another point which is no longer on the kite. The kite is *not symmetric* over this line.


[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A kite mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The kite has a point at negative six, negative six, a point at negative five, zero, a point at zero, negative five, and a point at eight, eight. The equation y equals negative X minus five is graphed on the coordinate plane. Dotted lines show the points locations after the reflection of the kite across the graphed line. The image falls outside the pre-image.

hints.content:
The symmetries that apply to the kite are:

Symmetry | Applies to the figure?
:- | :-:
Reflective symmetry over the line $y=x$ | Yes
Reflection symmetry over the line $y=-x-5$ | No
